reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address CoCrFeNiTi, short-range order, or precipitate strengthening in this system. E1 discusses dislocation behavior in a two-phase AlCoCrFeNi alloy, and E2 discusses nanotwinning in CrCoNi/CrMnFeCoNi, neither supporting the key premises about dislocation obstacles or heat-treatment effects in CoCrFeNiTi.
premises: Dislocation glide in pristine solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi encounters minimal intrinsic obstacles, leading to low hardness/strength and high plasticity.
Nano-scale short-range order or precipitates can act as effective dislocation pinning centers.
Inducing short-range order or precipitates via heat treatment in CoCrFeNiTi will increase hardness and strength.
